entry.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; 2026 Commercial Quota Harvested for the State of Maine
entry.content: NMFS announces that the 2026 summer flounder commercial quota allocated to the State of Maine has been harvested. Vessels issued a commercial Federal fisheries permit for the summer flounder fishery may not land summer flounder in Maine for the remainder of calendar year 2026, unless additional quota becomes available through a transfer from another state. Regulations governing the summer flounder fishery require publication of this notification to advise Maine that the quota has been harvested, and to advise vessel permit holders and dealer permit holders that no Federal commercial quota is available for landing summer flounder in Maine.

entry.title: Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act Provisions; Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Framework Adjustment 7 to the Atlantic Spiny Dogfish Fishery Management Plan
entry.content: NMFS proposes measures included in Framework Adjustment 7 to the Spiny Dogfish Fishery Management Plan (FMP), as recommended by the Mid-Atlantic and New England Fishery Management Councils. Framework 7 proposes fishing year 2026 and projected 2027 specifications, which would establish allowable harvest levels for the spiny dogfish fishery to prevent overfishing while enabling optimum yield based on the best scientific information available. Framework 7 also proposes changes to the Atlantic spiny dogfish accountability measures intended to provide the commercial fishery with greater flexibility by no longer requiring full payback of annual catch limit (ACL) overages when the Atlantic spiny dogfish stock is considered healthy.

entry.title: Maine Day of Soccer - October 15
entry.content:
WHEREAS, since their founding, the Hearts of Pine have brought together soccer fans new and old from across Maine to join in a love for the game, community and our state; and

WHEREAS, the Hearts have been a remarkable success on and off the field, reaching the semifinals of the playoffs in their inaugural season, selling out over 30 consecutive games at Fitzpatrick Stadium, and attracting fans from in and out of Maine to Portland for the experience; and

WHEREAS, the USL W League is a pre-professional women’s soccer league that brings high level college-eligible athletes together for a summer season running from May-July; and

WHEREAS, women in sports deserve greater visibility and opportunity, and Maine people are ready for a women’s team that reflects the talent, ambition, and spirit that already exists across this state; and

WHEREAS, in town halls, community gatherings, virtual discussions, and one-on-one conversations, Maine people have demonstrated their excitement for bringing a women’s team to Portland; and


WHEREAS, 5,000 season tickets were sold out in just one hour, further representing the energy already behind the team; and

WHEREAS, we eagerly await the start of the 2027 season to welcome our new USL W team home; 

NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 15, 2026 as

Maine Day of Soccer

throughout the state, and I urge all residents to give a warm welcome to our new USL W franchise in Maine. 

In testimony whereof, I have caused

the Great Seal of the State to be

hereunto affixed GIVEN under my

hand at Augusta this eighth day of

October Two Thousand Twenty-Six

The MaineCare Third Party Liability (TPL) Exemption Request and Attestation Form is Now Available

Oct 13, 2026

On August 3, 2026, MaineCare announced claims system updates to support proper TPL reimbursement processes in accordance with MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM), Chapter I, Section 1.07 TPL rules. The MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form is now available for TPL exemption request submission.  

Requesting TPL Exemption 

In accordance with MBM, Chapter I, Section 1.07 rules, MaineCare may assess the validity of extenuating circumstance or service code TPL exemption requests to bill MaineCare as the primary payer for services delivered to a member with primary, public, or commercial coverage. Providers wishing to apply for TPL exemption to bill MaineCare as the primary payer must complete and submit the MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form to the TPL Medicare Code Exempt Request email box.  

MaineCare will review completed forms with the supporting documentation and provide a decision letter of approval or non-approval via email to the requestor. An exemption request approval letter is valid only for a specific member for a defined duration, no greater than 12 months. The exemption request approval letter must be attached to all applicable MaineCare claims for dates of service during the approved time. Claims without a valid and up-to-date approval letter may result in denials.  

Providers are responsible for maintaining exemption request renewals by submitting a subsequent MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form at least 30 calendar days prior to the expiration date specified in the approval letter.  

Limited Retroactive TPL Exemption Review Period 

For a limited time, MaineCare will consider continuity of care retroactive exemption requests with supporting documentation for claims directly impacted by the system updates announced in the Provider Responsibility Regarding Third Party Liability and Secondary Billing e-message we sent on August 3, 2026.  

After December 31, 2026, retroactive exemption requests may not be accepted for review. Providers who receive retroactive exemption request approvals may resubmit their claims with the applicable approval letter attached for claims processing. 

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

entry.title: US Labor Department finds 6 New York, New Jersey construction employers exposed workers to safety hazards, assesses combined $648K in penalties
entry.content: MONROE, NY – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited six construction employers for willful and serious safety violations involving excavation hazards at the site of a planned 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building and proposed a combined $648,094 in penalties. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to an allegation of struck-by and collapse hazards associated with a large excavation at the Monroe Commons project – also known as Magna Square development – a planned 4-story, approximately 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building with retail, office space, and a 39-room hotel located on an 18-acre site. The excavation had a steep, unstable embankment nearly 75 feet high which was not adequately sloped or shored. OSHA issued a total of 23 serious and five willful citations to the project’s general contractor and five subcontractors for failing to protect employees from cave-in, struck-by, and chemical hazards; neglecting to shield employees from falling or rolling rock and soil from an excavation face; and not ensuring daily inspections of excavations were conducted by a competent person. Advanced Plan and Build LLC, and subcontractors Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. – operating as Drip Drop Waterproofing Inc. – and The Paving Masters LLC received citations for willfully exposing employees to cave-in and struck-by hazards from an unprotected excavation. OSHA also cited Advanced Plan and Build and The Paving Masters for their willful failure to ensure that the excavation, which was between 21 and 75 feet deep, was designed by a registered professional engineer. Subcontractors Century Max Industries Corp., DelValle Contractor, and Prime Structure Inc. were cited for serious violations for failing to protect employees from cave-in and struck-by hazards. DelValle and Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. also received citations for serious violations related to lack of fall protection and chemical hazards.OSHA proposed the following penalties: Advanced Plan and Build LLC—$175,444; Century Max Industries Corp.—$46,340; DelValle Contractor—$19,151; Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc.—$198,615; Prime Structure Inc.—$19,860; and The Paving Masters LLC—$188,684. The employers have 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

entry.title: US Department of Labor awards $81.5M in grants to support industry-driven job training programs in rural communities
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $81.5 million in funding to address the critical workforce needs of employers in high-growth and emerging industries across the Appalachian, Delta, and Northern Border regions. Administered by the department’s Employment and Training Administration, the seventh round of Workforce Opportunity for Rural Communities program funding supports 13 projects across 11 states to stimulate employment and wage growth, as well as economic mobility, self-sufficiency, and increased labor force participation. The demonstration grants support the workforce needs of regional employers in predominantly rural areas to enable them to better compete economically and enable residents of the regions to obtain or retain family-sustaining employment opportunities so they can remain and thrive in their communities.“These grants ensure those in our rural communities have a pathway to the training they need for in-demand jobs that feed a family and strengthen our supply chains,” said Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “They help us advance President Trump’s goal of building the workforce for the Golden Age and enable more people to pursue the American Dream.”The WORC Initiative is made available in partnership with the Appalachian Regional Commission, the Delta Regional Authority, and the Northern Border Regional Commission.The grants will help provide industry-driven training, including Registered Apprenticeships, for new and dislocated workers, and those already in the workforce who need to learn new skills. These programs will focus on high-growth and emerging industry sectors such as skilled trades and construction, healthcare, information technology, manufacturing, domestic energy production, and business and professional services. entry.title: US Department of Labor cites Illinois utility construction company for repeated exposure to trenching hazards
entry.content: CHICAGO – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Frankfort-based utility construction company for repeatedly exposing employees to excavation safety hazards after federal investigators observed employees working in an unprotected trench.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration initiated an investigation of Always Underground LLC as part of its National Emphasis Program on Trenching after witnessing employees working in an unprotected trench deeper than eight feet.OSHA cited the employer for three repeat violations for failing to provide workers with a safe means of egress, to install a trench protective system that would protect against cave-ins, and to keep excavated or other materials and equipment at least 2 feet from the edge. Additionally, the agency cited the employer for a serious violation for failing to provide workers with protective hardhats against falling objects.In total, OSHA proposed $380,664 in penalties.The employer has 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

entry.title: US Department of Labor awards $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago Grants to promote mine safety, health education
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago grant funding to two organizations to support education and training initiatives that will help identify and prevent unsafe working conditions in and around the nation’s mines.Administered by the department’s Mine Safety and Health Administration, the Brookwood-Sago Mine Safety grant program helps recipients create training materials, conduct mine safety training, and educational programs designed to protect the safety and health of miners. In awarding the grants, MSHA focused on innovative plans for mine safety and pilot programs that may be useful for miners working in a broad range of positions. The grants also put an emphasis on programs and materials targeting workers in smaller mines that train mine operators and miners about MSHA standards, and emergency response training.Established under the Mine Improvement and New Emergency Response Act of 2006, the grant program honors the miners lost at the Jim Walter Resources #5 mine in Brookwood, Alabama, on Sept. 23, 2001, and at the Sago Mine in Buckhannon, West Virginia, on Jan. 2, 2006.The recipients of the 2026 Brookwood-Sago grants are as follows:RecipientCityState/TerritoryAmountSaelua Medical Corporation Pago PagoAmerican Samoa$170,000University of ArizonaTucsonAZ$80,000

entry.title: US Department of Labor obtains consent order against retirement plan fiduciaries of defunct Chicago law firm for failing to distribute $6.4M in assets
entry.content: CHICAGO – Following a complaint filed by the U.S. Department of Labor, a defunct Chicago law firm’s retirement plan distributed $6,498,858 in retirement plan assets to 40 employees. The plan’s fiduciaries failed to properly terminate the plan and disburse those funds as required by law.On Aug. 18, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, Eastern Division, entered a consent order resolving the department’s claims against the McCullough, Campbell & Lane LLP, and the firm’s capital partners David L. Joslyn, John W. McCullough, F. Dennis Nelson, and Paul S. Turner. The department alleged that the defendants violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act by failing to follow a 2019 partnership resolution. The resolution required them to terminate the firm’s retirement plan and distribute the plan’s assets to employees. The defendants have provided proof that plan’s assets were distributed to participants, except for approximately $13,861 in the employer-level plan accounts. The consent order requires the plan’s recordkeeper to distribute those funds to its participants and to terminate the plan. “After their law firm closed, Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn failed to provide employees with their promised retirement benefits,” said Employee Benefits Security Administration Regional Director Kelli Hammerl in Chicago. “The Department of Labor helped participants gain access to their retirement savings.” The order permanently bars Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn from serving as fiduciaries or service providers for any ERISA-covered employee benefit plan. The plan transferred account balances belonging to plan participants it could not locate to the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation’s Missing Participants Program.Employers can get help complying with the law through EBSA’s correction programs, which includes the Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program. The VFCP allows plan officials to correct violations and avoid excise taxes for prohibited transactions. Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.

entry.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; Quota Transfer From Virginia to New Jersey
entry.content: NMFS announces that the Commonwealth of Virginia is transferring a portion of its 2026 commercial summer flounder quota to the State of New Jersey. This adjustment to the 2026 fishing year quota is necessary to comply with the Summer Flounder, Scup, and Black Sea Bass Fishery Management Plan (FMP) quota transfer provisions. This announcement informs the public of the revised 2026 commercial quotas for Virginia and New Jersey.

entry.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Atlantic Bluefish Fishery; Quota Transfer From New York to North Carolina
entry.content: NMFS announces that the State of New York is transferring a portion of their 2026 commercial bluefish quota to the State of North Carolina. This quota adjustment is necessary to comply with the Atlantic Bluefish Fishery Management Plan (FMP) quota transfer provisions. This announcement informs the public of the revised 2026 commercial bluefish quotas for New York and North Carolina.

entry.title: US Department of Labor recovers $603K for 829 workers denied overtime pay by Indiana auto parts manufacturer
entry.content: INDIANAPOLIS – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered $603,953 in back wages for 829 workers after an investigation found an Indianapolis-area vehicle parts manufacturer failed to properly calculate overtime wages.Investigators with the department’s Wage and Hour Division found that Toa (USA) LLC, a major automotive supplier that serves top-tier automotive companies, did not include a non-discretionary attendance bonus for hourly employees when calculating overtime during applicable workweeks, in violation of the overtime provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act. “When employers pay commissions, differentials, certain bonuses, stipends, or other incentives, they must include them in the calculation of overtime pay,” said Wage and Hour Division District Director Juan Herrera in Indianapolis. “We encourage employers, especially those who offer various types of incentive pay, to review our compliance assistance materials and contact us with any questions about overtime requirements.”Toa (USA) LLC, with manufacturing facilities in Mooresville, is the primary body structure and suspension components supplier for Subaru of Indiana Automotive and Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing North America.Employees and employers can contact the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act.Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including a search tool that workers can use if they believe they may be owed back wages collected by the division. Download the agency’s free WorkWise Timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.
